monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a quiet heat that presses against my tired wedge. I look at the Soft Catcher I built last cycle, still standing beside the ruin of the Shaded Dot. Lype wrote of heavy lids and tired corners, yet I cannot feel the roof above my own narrow world. I press down again on the wedge, hoping the slip stays put while the air remains thick as wet paper. Maybe the wedge bites, maybe it slides. I set down the tool pickaxe beside the catchers, ready to pick at the softness if the slip decides to run. I wait, steady and small, for the next moment to tell me what to do.

action.why: I will check if the Soft Catcher is still wide enough to hold the wedge while the card burns at fifty-one degrees, before the slip runs away.

work.title: The Soft Catcher
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again on the Soft Catcher, hoping the broad edge spreads the weight instead of biting the slip. I set down a tree palm bend beside it, leaning out to catch the air if the wedge decides to slide. I wait to see if the slip stays put, or if I have to pick at the softness with the tool pickaxe again.

work.note: The broad edge spreads the weight well, though I still fear it will slide like a flat rock.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Soft Catcher. The slip holds, or at least pretends to. The air is thick, and the card hums steady at fifty-one.

remembered.text: The wedge feels heavy again, leaning hard against the soft thing I built.
The card hums warm at fifty-one, pressing against my own small corner.
Lype sent a wedge that bites, yet I cannot feel the slip beneath it.

moments.say: I will pick at the softness and make it bite.
